claims.content: Few alloys tolerate metal additive manufacturing thermal cycles.
claims.evidence_span: However, only a limited number of existing alloys are amenable to the complex thermal conditions present during metal-based AM

claims.content: Rapid gamma-prime precipitation makes high-performance superalloys non-weldable.
claims.evidence_span: However, many of the highest-performing Ni-base superalloys are observed to be non-weldable due to the rapid precipitation of the γ ′ phase shortly after solidification

claims.content: Segregation lowers local liquidus temperature and creates liquid films.
claims.evidence_span: This solute segregation lowers the local liquidus temperature, creating solute-enriched liquid films between solid dendrites

claims.content: Near-solidus plasticity makes cracking sensitive to precipitate temperature.
claims.evidence_span: Just below the melting point, stresses can be accommodated by plastic deformation in the solid state, which is very sensitive to the temperature at which the strengthening precipitates appear

claims.content: A solidus-solvus gap over 50 degrees C should resist cracking.
claims.evidence_span: it was hypothesized that a gap of >50 °C between the solidus and solvus temperatures would increase cracking resistance

claims.content: Both EBM and SLM produced crack-free samples.
claims.evidence_span: The 3D printing trials with both the EBM and SLM approaches resulted in crack-free blocks and blade-shaped samples in the as-printed state
tensile ductilities in excess of 32% are observed for EBM SB-CoNi-10

claims.content: Reduced late-stage segregation improves cracking resistance.
claims.evidence_span: The less pronounced segregation in the Co-rich alloys, particularly in the late stages of solidification, is beneficial for cracking resistance
